test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 29 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: In which of the following states was the Skill Development Centre inaugurated under the ‘Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram’ scheme in July 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A state-of-the-art **Skill Development Centre** was inaugurated in the state of **Kerala** in **July 2025** to enhance the employability of the local youth under the **Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram (PMJVK)**.
 
• The **Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram** is a **Centrally Sponsored Scheme** implemented by the **Ministry of Minority Affairs** across India to provide better socio-economic infrastructure.
 
• The inauguration in **Kerala** specifically targets the creation of specialized **infrastructure** for **vocational training**, ensuring that students and workers from **minority communities** have access to modern industrial skills. ***Hence, the correct answer is Kerala.***
 
• This initiative is designed to address the **development deficits** in identified areas by providing facilities for **education**, **skill development**, and **healthcare**.
 
• The **Skill Development Centre** is expected to offer courses aligned with the **National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF)**, focusing on sectors like **Information Technology**, **Electronics**, and **Healthcare**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram (PMJVK):**
 
 
• The scheme was restructured and renamed from the **Multi-sectoral Development Programme (MsDP)** in **May 2018** to provide a sharper focus on the development of **Minority Concentration Areas (MCAs)**.
 
• It aims to improve the **quality of life** of people and reduce imbalances in **Minority Concentration Areas** through the creation of **community assets**.
 
• The **Ministry of Minority Affairs** is the nodal agency responsible for the planning and execution of projects under this **Centrally Sponsored Scheme**.
 
• Projects are approved based on the proposals submitted by **State Governments** and **Union Territory** administrations, ensuring a bottom-up approach to development.
 
 
 
• **Funding and Coverage:**
 
 
• The funding pattern for **PMJVK** generally follows a **60:40** ratio between the **Centre** and the **State**, while for **North-Eastern** and **Himalayan States**, it is **90:10**.
 
• The scheme covers **all districts** of the country, focusing on blocks, towns, and clusters of villages where the **minority population** is **25%** or more, along with backwardness in **socio-economic** parameters.
 
• Identified minority communities include **Muslims**, **Sikhs**, **Christians**, **Buddhists**, **Jains**, and **Zoroastrians (Parsis)** as notified under the **National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Strategic Objectives:**
 
 
• One of the primary objectives is to ensure **inclusive growth** by providing **Skill Development** hubs that reduce the **unemployment rate** among marginalized sections.
 
• The scheme supports the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** (Self-Reliant India) mission by fostering **entrepreneurship** and providing **technical training** at the grassroots level.
 
• In **Kerala**, the focus of such centers often includes **nursing**, **paramedical sciences**, and **digital literacy**, reflecting the state's high demand for skilled professionals in these sectors.
 
• **July 2025** marks a significant timeline for the completion of several **PMJVK** projects sanctioned during the previous fiscal years to ensure **last-mile delivery** of government services.
